newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian president formally calls election.
newsitem.headline: Albanian president formally calls election.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha on Friday formally called general elections for the troubled Balkan state for June 29, his office said.
He called the elections although most political parties have threatened to boycott the poll.

"The president of the republic...decreed today the dissolution of the National Assembly before the end of its mandate and the holding of new parliamentary elections on Sunday June 29, 1997," Berisha's office said in a statement.

The early elections are seen the key element in restoring order in Albania after the country was torn apart by riots in February and March after the collapse of pyramid investment schemes bankrupted thousands of people.
Most political parties are threatening to boycott the poll in a dispute over the election law, which they say favours Berisha.

European Union envoy Franz Vranitzky seemed to have broken the deadlock on Thursday by persuading parliament to draft a new election law but the parties later said they still did not like the legislation.
